verdicts.title: What a run costs is never stated before the first bill: not in the ad, the policy step, the handbook, or on the Run button
verdicts.why: Reproduced in release.html by reading the text off the page. The ad says only 'Outcome-based pricing. Pay for outcomes and the compute required to deliver them.' and 'Usage is billed on Fridays, even while idle'. The policy step has three lines and no amount. The handbook row says 'pay usage on Friday' and 'Idle weeks still bill', no amount. After buying, the button reads 'Run agents · 0 energy · 0 slots · billed Friday' and the only weekly figure in the panel is 'Idle weeks still bill $150–$300'. '$249' occurs nowhere in the shipping file (grep: 0). Rules re-read (src/game/claink.js:43-47, 287-288, 350): a $0 run bills 249 + 2..5 x 140..280, so $529 to $1,649. My own arithmetic over 400,000 draws from those constants (tariff.mjs): median usage $977, median invoice with the 10% overage $1,018; a new run that buys in week 1 has $100 left after salary and rent, so 40.6% of $0 first runs end the first Friday at -$1,000 or lower and 2.4% in Collections. The auditor's figures (980, 1,020, 40.9%, 2.7%) hold. Not a recorded decision: the 2.1 implementation brief lists these very rates and says 'Clarify actual terms with dynamic values' (docs/2.1/TTST_2.1_Claude_Code_Implementation.md, section C), and help.js's own header says every number in the handbook comes from the game; the approved sentences (copydeck 295, 362-365) simply never carried the rate. A player is misled by omission: the one weekly figure in sight is about a quarter of what the button bills.
verdicts.smallest_fix: One sentence of rates, built from the CLAINK constants, in ONE place a player reads before paying. Least code: the handbook row, src/copy/help.js:51 ('pay usage on Friday: $249 a run plus $140–$280 per billed outcome (two to five on a $0 run)' and 'Idle weeks still bill $150–$300'), with four fields added to handbookFacts (src/game/selectors.js:120) and to the lint sample V. The 2.1.1 working copy has already taken the other route (CK_AD.policy in src/copy/clainkUi.js, commit 86eb228: rates, true-up and cancel fee in the policy step, with a fit step so Accept stays in sight); that closes this finding too. Do not add a clause to the Run button or the usage line as well, and leave the ad and its fine print as vague as they are.
verdicts.regression_risk: Both places are approved copydeck sentences (lines 295, 362-364): an added sentence needs an 'owner' note in docs/2.1/copy-coverage-notes.json and lint samples for the new parameters. Handbook route, measured by injecting the sentence into the frozen page: the clAInk row goes 156 to 176 px and the dialog 849 to 859 px of its 876 px limit at 1440x900 (no scroll); 918 to 944 of 1056 at 1920x1080; the 2.1.1 working copy's handbook is already longer than 2.1's, so re-measure there. Policy route: the step was 367 px at 1280x720 with a ceiling of 68% of a 646 px column (439 px), so two more wrapped terms do not fit without a fit step, and Accept and Not now must still be in sight at 1280x720 and on a 320 px phone. No rule, price, dice or save changes.

verdicts.title: On laptop-height windows, pressing Run agents lands the strike card, 'Closed: $0' and the Friday estimate out of sight, and the workspace does not follow
verdicts.why: Reproduced in the shipping file with real presses on ck-active-0-strikes.json (week 2, four deals; test-results/audit/check-claink/run.cjs). 1280x720, three runs: strike card 0 px in sight every time, 'Closed: $0' 0, 7 and 24 of 24 px (under the fade), the estimate 0 px, scrollTop 0. 1366x768, three runs: card 34 of 76, 45 of 99 and 77 of 99 px, the line that says what it took 0 to 5 of 18 px, estimate 0 px. 1440x900: whole. With scripted dice in test.html a churn strike ('-$6,600 closed · -$792 commission clawed back') shows 0 px of its card at 1280x720, 1366x768, 1536x730 and 1440x790 and is whole at 1920x950, while the log says only 'Strike 2/3 (Customer Success): A customer upgraded to 3x, then churned.' Third strike at 1280x720: true-up line 5 of 18 px, REVOKED card 0 px. A hand scroll survives End week (scrollTop 152 at 1280x720, 86 at 1366x768; 'Run agents' 0 of 38 px in sight the next week). matrix.cjs:183 does scroll the card into view by script before checking it. This is the common case, not an edge: 650 to 800 px is the window height most laptops give a browser, the report is staged beat by beat, and its last beats (the result, what it took, what Friday will charge) land under the fade. Not a recorded decision: CHANGELOG.md:42 records the fade at the fold, but the release notes (line 43) say 'On an early board a run's whole report shows, strike card and all', which fails on this board below 1440x900 (QA evidence 18 itself lists 404/508 and 356/508 there), and the same changelog calls 'you pressed the link and saw no buttons' a defect.
verdicts.smallest_fix: src/ui/ClainkUi.jsx, ClainkConsole, beside the cancel question's rule (line 348): remember that the player pressed Run agents (its onClick, line 475); in a layout effect, while that report plays and once when it ends, set the workspace's own scrollTop (only where scrollHeight exceeds clientHeight, never the page's) so the newest line and then the card and the estimate are in sight; set it back to 0 when s.week changes. No CSS, no copy. Tried in the page on test.html (foot.cjs): with the workspace at its foot after a run, the card, what it took, the manager's note, the estimate and 'Cancel seat' are all whole at 1280x720 and 1366x768 (picture: foot-ck-active-1-strike@1280x720.png). Add one layout check that presses the button with scripted dice and asserts the card and the estimate in sight without a scripted scroll. The 2.1.1 working copy holds an uncommitted version of this (read, not run).
verdicts.regression_risk: After a run on a short window the status line (where focus is put), the spent button, the strike boxes and, at two strikes, the red warning scroll out until the week turns; the title bar is sticky and the card repeats the count. At about 650 px tall a harmful card plus the manager's note is taller than the room: at the foot the card's heading shows 10 of 18 px, so stop at the card's top there (measured: card, note and estimate then whole). The reset on a new week also undoes a hand scroll, which is an improvement but a change. Reduced motion gets a jump. Stacked layouts and windows from 1440x900 up must stay untouched (no inner scroll there). The layout gate's dock states are loaded, not pressed, so they see nothing either way, and matrix.cjs:183's scripted scroll would hide a regression. UI only: no rule, dice, save or copy.

verdicts.title: End week's Friday preview lists salary and rent but not the clAInk invoice
verdicts.why: Reproduced in release.html by hovering End week. With a seat that ran and $669 due the hint reads 'End week. Friday: salary +$1,000, energy +15, stress -4. Friday events and collections may change this.'; the same with an idle seat that will bill $150–$300 (ck-active-2-strikes.json); with rent due it reads 'salary +$1,000, rent -$1,600, ...' (fresh.json). The selector calls itself 'the parts of Friday that are certain' (src/game/selectors.js:57), and the invoice is charged on every Friday the run survives outside week 13 (src/game/week.js:135, claink.js:368-378). At 1366x768 and 1280x720 the workspace's own estimate is below its fold at load (0 of 36 px), so the hint is the only Friday summary in sight there. Not a recorded decision: the copydeck's instruction for this hint (line 92: 'keep actual salary, rent if due, energy/stress forecast') describes what 2.0.1 showed and is silent on clAInk. A player with a seat reads a Friday that is $150 to $1,649 better than the one they get, on the button they press every week, and 2.1.1 has just made this hint the place that speaks about cash and Collections.
verdicts.smallest_fix: src/game/selectors.js, fridayPreview: add the seat's charge for an active seat outside the week 13 freeze (c.due if the agents ran this week, otherwise the CLAINK.IDLE range, shown and not rolled). src/copy/ui.js:103, HINT.endWeek: one clause after rent, ', clAInk -$669' or ', clAInk -$150–$300'. Nothing else (not the Cash card).
verdicts.regression_risk: The hint is brief section 1's: 2.1.1 already rewrote HINT.endWeek to say when salary and rent alone reach Collections, so the clause has to sit with that sentence, and that warning still ignores the invoice (leave that as it is rather than widen scope; 'Friday events and collections may change this' covers it, and the overage). Length: injected into the frozen page, the longest form (rent plus an idle range) still takes two lines at 1280, 1100 and 1026 px wide. Kpis.jsx:45 reads the same selector (a new field is harmless). The copy lint needs a sample carrying the new field; test/engine/rng.test.mjs:91 calls fridayPreview to prove selectors roll no dice, so the idle amount must stay a range. No save or seeded behaviour.

verdicts.title: The handbook no longer says a strike can do damage, and words the true-up less plainly than 2.0.1 did
verdicts.why: Both texts confirmed in the shipped files. 2.0.1 (test/baseline/v2.0.1/index.html): '...earn a strike, sometimes with damage. Strike 3: seat revoked, a deal walks, and a true-up takes all your cash plus $200–1,800'. 2.1, read off release.html: 'every $0 run earns a strike. ... Third strike revokes the seat, may cost a live deal, and charges a true-up based on cash plus $200–$1,800'. No string in release.html says a strike can do damage before one does (grep 'sometimes with|real damage': 0), and the rule is 38% of strikes 1 and 2 (claink.js:34, 303). But the 2.1 sentence is the approved copydeck's, word for word (deck line 295; copy-coverage-notes L295: 'The approved sentences are rendered from the live configuration'), nothing in it is false, the strike card states exactly what an incident took when it happens, and the README carries the warning. The true-up half is a preference: 'based on cash plus $200–$1,800' is accurate and the two-strike note gives the exact landing range. The damage half is a real but slight gap inside approved copy, so it is the owner's call, not a defect.
verdicts.smallest_fix: Leave alone unless the owner wants it. If so, four words only, in src/copy/help.js:51: 'every $0 run earns a strike, sometimes with real damage.', with an 'owner' note at L295 in docs/2.1/copy-coverage-notes.json. Leave the true-up clause as approved.
verdicts.regression_risk: A deviation from an approved copydeck sentence, so the coverage note for L295 must say so. Measured by injecting the words into the frozen page: no extra line at 1440x900, 1366x768 or 1280x720 (the row stays 156 px), one more line at 1920x1080 (dialog 918 to 928 of 1056). The 2.1.1 working copy's handbook is already longer than 2.1's, so re-measure there. No test or script quotes the row (grep over test/ and scripts/).

verdicts.title: 'A live deal may walk' at two strikes, but the rule always takes your most advanced deal
verdicts.why: Rule re-read: clainkRevoke takes [...s.deals].sort(ckRank)[0] with no roll (src/game/claink.js:266-267), so with any deal on the board the most advanced one always goes. Scripted third strike in test.html on ck-active-2-strikes.json: the $18,000 Proposal at the top of the list left (4 open, $40,000 became 3 open, $22,000). The note above the button read 'Next $0 run is strike 3: seat revoked, a live deal may walk, ...' with four deals on the board. 2.0.1's shipped file says 'a deal walks'. So the note understates a certainty. It is on record as a decision, though: the copydeck (line 368) says 'Replace "a deal walks" with "a live deal may walk" if pipeline can be empty', and copy-coverage-notes L368 records "'a deal walks' became 'a live deal may walk'". The misreading is slight: the note's weight is the revocation and the true-up, which it states exactly, and 'may' is not false.
verdicts.smallest_fix: If taken: src/copy/clainkUi.js:52, CK_STRIKES.hotHead takes whether the board has a deal; src/ui/ClainkUi.jsx:259-268 and :479 pass s.deals.length>0. With a deal, the deck's own 'a deal walks'; with none, 'a live deal may walk' as now. Both wordings are the copydeck's (line 368), so only the L368 note changes. Leave the 'may' in the policy step and the handbook, which speak before there is a board. Not the auditor's 'your most advanced deal walks', which is new copy. (The 2.1.1 working copy holds exactly this, uncommitted.)
verdicts.regression_risk: The with-deal sentence is shorter, so the note cannot gain a line (it is three lines at 1280 wide and on phones). The coverage note for L368 and a lint sample for the new argument must be updated; no test or script asserts the old sentence (grep). Display only: no save, dice or rule.

verdicts.title: At 1366x768 and 1280x720 'Cancel seat' and the usage line sit below the workspace's fold once any report is showing
verdicts.why: Measured at load in release.html, nothing scrolled (run.cjs load, five states, three sizes). 1440x900: the usage line and 'Cancel seat' whole in all five. 1366x768: whole before the first run; with a report showing 'Cancel seat' starts 23 to 77 px below the fold. 1280x720: 'Cancel seat' 14 of 16 px before the first run and 71 to 162 px below the fold with a report showing. The auditor's numbers are right. But this is the dock as designed and recorded: the workspace keeps its share and scrolls inside it, fading at the fold (CHANGELOG.md:42; QA report section 8, item 20); the changelog itself says the link's question 'opens at the foot of the workspace, which could be below the fold' and chose to bring only the question into sight (line 43); QA evidence 18 lists these overflows (idle 349/373 at 1280x720; after a run 404/508 and 356/508). The link is one scroll away, the fade says there is more, the handbook states the cancel terms, and a quiet exit is in character for the vendor. The only remedy on offer is a reorder that changes the idle workspace at every size.
verdicts.smallest_fix: Leave alone. If finding 2 is taken, the foot of the workspace, 'Cancel seat' included, is in sight after every run (tried in the page at 1280x720 and 1366x768: whole), which is the moment a player weighs cancelling.
verdicts.regression_risk: None if left. The proposed reorder would move the usage line and the link above last week's report at every size, and the cancel question's scroll rule (ClainkUi.jsx:348) aims at the foot, so it would have to be re-aimed and dock-question-seen proved again.

verdicts.title: When the workspace scrolls it shows the browser's default 15 px scrollbar, the only unstyled one in the game
verdicts.why: Reproduced in release.html with Chromium's scrollbars left on (bar.cjs). At 1280x720 and 1366x768 the workspace is 496 or 530 px wide with 481 or 515 px of content: a 15 px classic bar with arrow buttons, scrollbar-width 'auto', running down the vendor's panel directly under the log, whose bar is 10 px, thin and themed, as is the deal list's (pictures: bar-shipped-ck-report-strike-hurt@1366x768.png, bar-shipped-page-ck-active-2-strikes@1280x720.png). At laptop heights the workspace scrolls from the first run on (508 px of content in 356 to 404), so players on Windows and Linux see it for most of a run. With the proposed rule injected into the page the bar is 10 px in the panel's own line colour. One correction: it is not the only unstyled bar in the game. The handbook dialog scrolls at laptop heights with the same default bar (17 px at 1366x768, bar-handbook@1366x768.png); that is outside this area and worth passing on. The finding stands for the workspace because it is on the main screen all week beside two themed bars. No document mentions it; every QA picture and gate hides scrollbars. Seen in Linux Chromium only: on Windows the default bar may be drawn dark, but it is still the wide classic one.
verdicts.smallest_fix: src/styles/claink.css, on the docked .claink-console rule (line 247, or 99-100): scrollbar-width:thin;scrollbar-color:var(--ck-line) transparent. One pair of declarations, clAInk's own token, the same pattern as .scroll in app.css:124. (Already in the 2.1.1 working copy, uncommitted.)
verdicts.regression_risk: While the workspace scrolls, its content is 5 px wider in browsers that draw scrollbars (measured: clientWidth 481 to 486 at 1280x720), which can move a line break: in the two-strike state the content went from 521 px, which is what such players get today, to 503 px, which is what the headless gates already measure. So it moves real browsers toward what was verified. Gates and QA pictures hide scrollbars, so nothing asserted changes. macOS overlay bars and touch are unaffected; a browser without these properties keeps today's bar. var(--ck-line) is a quiet thumb on that panel, as quiet as the deal list's; var(--ck-mut) is the other token on hand if it reads too faint.

missed.title: The audit's smallest desktop window is taller than a real small laptop's: at 1366x650 the workspace has about 220 to 255 px under its title bar
missed.where: src/styles/claink.css:216-218 and :250 (the desktop dock applies down to 620 px tall); src/ui/ClainkUi.jsx:120-124 (dockRoom)
missed.evidence: A 1366x768 screen gives a browser about 1366x650, and the auditor measured nothing between 720 and 600 px tall. In release.html and test.html at 1366x650 (run.cjs, foot.cjs under test-results/audit/check-claink/): right after buying, before any run, the usage line and 'Cancel seat' are already below the fold (355 px of content in a 279 px box); after a scripted $0 run only 67 of the report's 171 px show, 'Closed: $0' and the strike card 0 px, and the estimate starts 180 px below the fold (527 px in 264). With the workspace put at its foot in the page, a harmful strike with the manager's note is taller than the room: the card shows 82 of 99 px and its heading 10 of 18; aimed at the card's top instead, the card, the note and the estimate are whole and 'Cancel seat' shows 14 of 16. The ad and its policy step do fit there, price line, button and fine print in sight (short-ad@1366x650.png). Seen in passing and outside this area: at this height 2.1's End week button is off the screen (y 681 to 717 in a 650 px window that does not scroll); the 2.1.1 working copy's commit b95caa7 is about that.
missed.proposal: No change of its own: it is finding 2, only worse, and the main reason to take that fix. Check the fix at one window in this band (1366x650) as well as at 1280x720, and let the scroll stop at the card's top when the card, the manager's note and the estimate do not all fit.

missed.title: The policy step's three terms are a list with no markers, and on a phone they run together
missed.where: src/styles/claink.css:92-93 (.claink-policy ul reserves 16 px for bullets); src/styles/base.css:6 (ol,ul{list-style:none} takes them away)
missed.evidence: release.html, fresh.json, the policy step: computed list-style-type is 'none' on the list and on each item while its padding-left is 16px. At 1440x900 each term is one line and it reads as three indented lines (policy@1440x900.png). At 390x844 each term wraps to two lines, and at 320x568 to two or three, with 2 px between terms, so the terms the player is about to accept read as one block of six to eight lines (policy@390x844.png in my folder; the auditor's own shots/ad-policy@320x568.clip.png).
missed.proposal: One declaration in clAInk's stylesheet: .claink-policy ul{list-style:disc} (optionally li::marker in var(--ck-mut)). The marker sits in the 16 px already reserved, so no line break moves. The 2.1.1 working copy already has it (commit 86eb228); keep it, and it matters more there because the policy now has five terms.
